title: A Multiline Study of a High-mass Young Stellar Object in the Small Magellanic Cloud with ALMA: The Detection of Methanol Gas at 0.2 Solar Metallicity
question: What are the physical and chemical properties of dense cores around a high-mass YSO in the SMC, and is CH3OH gas present at 0.2 solar metallicity?

what.value: Dust mass absorption coefficient for grains with thin ice mantles

evidence.quote: is the mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles as taken from (cite: Oss94)

what.value: 32S/33S = 40 from 33SO2 in an LMC hot core

evidence.quote: We here assume $^{32}$S/$^{33}$S = 40, based on the $^{33}$SO$_2$ observations towards a hot core in the LMC (cite: ST16b).
We here assume $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C = 50 according to HCO$^+$/H$^{13}$CO$^+$ observations of the N27 region in the SMC (cite: Hei99).
(cite: Mar89) reported $N_{\mathrm{H}}$/$E(B-V)$ = 4.6 $\times$ 10$^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$ mag$^{-1}$ for the SMC.

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and continuum at three positions
recipe.method: Spectra and continuum flux extracted from 0.34″ diameter regions at P1, P2, P3 after uvcontsub
Single Gaussian fits with optional polynomial local baseline; direct integration for two narrow CH3OH lines; 3 sigma detection criterion
Rotation diagram under optically thin LTE, straight-line fit, spectroscopy from CDMS
key_parameters: Blended 241.90416 GHz line intensity divided by two

recipe.goal: H2 column density and mass from dust continuum
recipe.method: Optically thin dust emission with Ossenkopf & Henning opacity, dust-to-gas ratio 1/5 of 0.008
assumptions: Dust temperature equals CH3OH rotation temperature at P2/P3

recipe.goal: Column densities and abundances of other molecules
recipe.method: Solve rotation-diagram equation for N at assumed T; isotopologues for optically thick lines

evidence.quote: The measured continuum brightnesses are 0.30 mJy/beam for P1, 0.16 mJy/beam for P2, and 0.06 mJy/beam for P3.

answer_key.quantity: Gas mass YSO core / East core

evidence.quote: about 80 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ for the YSO core and about 50 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ for the East core
The bolometric luminosity of the YSO is estimated to be 2 $\times$ 10$^4$ L$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ by integrating the SED from 1 $\mu$m to 1200 $\mu$m.

Line-free channels used for uvcontsub and the continuum bandwidth

Velocity ranges for moment maps and polynomial order of baseline fits
Rest frequency/velocity reference for channel maps and how rotation diagram uncertainties were derived (fitting method)

score_reason: Public data and clear analysis equations, but imaging parameters and fitting details are missing.
